title: Showcase: formal debate and the book
summary: Debate Rebut across three formal rounds on the motion you pick, then talk about the season book and run the teach-someone-younger quest.

steps.title: A formal debate, and the book
steps.body:
This is the season's last debate against Rebut, and it is formal: three full rounds, recorded start to finish, no pausing to think off camera. Pick your motion before you start, either 'Zoos should exist' or 'It is better to be smart than kind'. This quest is set up for zoos, so if you want the other motion, ask a grown-up to switch it for you before you begin.

Steelman first, same rule as every debate this season, but hold yourself to it more strictly this time: before you make your own point in round 1, say the strongest version of the other side's argument, in your own words, the real one, not a weak one you can knock down easily. Only after that do you give your own claim, reason and example.

Round 2, ask one cross-examination question that finds a real gap in the other side. Round 3, make your strongest closing point, one point said once, not three points stacked on top of each other.

When the debate ends, spend five minutes talking about the book you read this season. Say one specific thing it changed about how you think, not just that you liked it, and one favourite moment, a scene or a line you can describe in enough detail that someone who has not read it could picture it. Open the book talk by naming the title and why you picked it up, and close it by saying whether you would recommend it to a friend and why.

steps.title: Teach someone younger
steps.body:
A parent card is the short card in the app that a grown-up normally uses with Sprout. It has a title, a list of three to five steps to do together, and two or three "things to notice" while you do them.

This week you are the one running it, not a grown-up, same as showcase weeks 4 and 8. Open this week's Sprout parent card from Sprout's screen, and read it once, all the way through, before you start, so you know what is supposed to happen.

Then run the card with a younger sibling, cousin or friend, or a parent playing the part. Let them do the actual activity, the sorting, the counting, the pattern, whatever the card asks for. Your job is to read the prompts and notice what they do, not to do it for them.

Watch for one thing they do that surprises you, something they get right that you did not expect, or a way they solve it that is not how you would have.
checklist: I let them do it, I did not do it for them
I noticed one thing they could do that surprised me

steps.title: Record it
steps.prompt: Record the full formal debate, all three rounds, and the five minutes about the book, phone propped up, whole face in frame.
